parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the amplitude modulation (AM) of a radio wave.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A radio wave is modulated by an audio signal.

The variation with frequency *f* of the amplitude of the modulated wave is shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Determine:
parts.text: the wavelength of the carrier wave

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the bandwidth of the modulated wave

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: the maximum frequency of the audio signal.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The power of a radio signal at a transmitter is *P*ₜ.
At a receiver, the received power *P*ᵣ is given by the expression

$P_\mathrm{R} = \frac{0.082P_\mathrm{T}}{x^2}$

where *x* is the distance, in metres, between the transmitter and the receiver.

For the transmission of this signal, the attenuation is 73 dB.

Determine the distance *x*.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A graph of amplitude against frequency, showing a peak at 300 kHz and smaller modulated-wave peaks between 292 kHz and 308 kHz.
